He ascended a throne at age two in 1908, then later reigned as a puppet emperor for a wartime Japanese state and was held as a war criminal until 1959 — which last emperor of China is he?
Puyi: Emperor of China (1908–1912) and of Manchukuo (1934–1945)
Also known as the Baader-Meinhof Group, this West German far-left militant group waged a campaign of bombings, kidnappings, and shootouts with police from 1970 until 1998 — which organization is it?
Red Army Faction: West German far-left militant organisation (1970–1998). The RAF described itself as a communist and anti-imperialist urban guerrilla group.
A national hero who led his country through the First War of Scottish Independence, this descendant of King David I reigned as King of Scots from 1306 until 1329 — who was he?

Robert the Bruce: King of Scotland from 1306 to 1329. As Earl of Carrick, Robert the Bruce supported his family's claim to the Scottish throne and took part in William Wallace's campaign against Edward I of England.

Held on March 17, the traditional death date of the foremost patron saint of Ireland, this religious and cultural holiday was made an official Christian feast day in the early 17th century. What day is it?
Signs of the coming of Judgement Day

Saint Patrick's Day: Cultural and religious celebration on 17 March. The day commemorates Saint Patrick and the arrival of Christianity in Ireland, and, by extension, celebrates the heritage and culture of the Irish in general.

It began in August 1999 after Islamist fighters crossed from Chechnya into Dagestan, followed by deadly apartment bombings in Russian cities, and dragged on in the North Caucasus until April 2009 — which conflict?

Second Chechen War: 1999–2009 conflict in Chechnya and the North Caucasus. Russian authorities were quick to blame Chechens for the bombings, although no Chechen, field commander or otherwise, took responsibility for the attacks.
Born Szymon Perski, this Israeli statesman served twice as prime minister and later as president, sitting in the Knesset for 48 years across a 70-year career — who is he?
Known as 'Mother of Modern China,' this wife of Sun Yat-sen became the only female, non-Communist head of state the People's Republic ever had — who was she?
Soong Ching-ling: Wife of Sun Yat-sen (1893–1981)
Known at home as the 'Great Power Era,' this 17th-century Baltic dominion began with Gustavus Adolphus's ascension in 1611 and collapsed after the Great Northern War in 1721 — which power?
Swedish Empire: Historical period in the history of Sweden (1611–1721)

Known in Hebrew as the Shoah, this World War II genocide killed roughly six million people — about two-thirds of Europe's Jewish population — through mass shootings and gas chambers at camps like Auschwitz-Birkenau. What is it?
The Holocaust: Genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany.
This British Labour politician sat in the Commons for 47 of 51 years and later presided over the Stop the War Coalition — though for a stretch he was known as The Viscount Stansgate — who is he?
Tony Benn: British politician and activist (1925–2014)
This Portuguese nobleman opened the first direct sea route from Europe to India, rounding the Cape of Good Hope and crossing the Indian Ocean from Malindi in Kenya to Kozhikode. Who is he?
As East Germany's chief decision-maker for two decades, this communist leader demanded the construction of the Berlin Wall in 1961 despite Soviet reluctance — who was he?
Walter Ulbricht: Leader of East Germany from 1950 to 1971.
The New York Times once called him the country's best-known lawyer; this civil rights attorney is most famous for defending the Chicago Seven — who is it?
Harold Alexander, 1st Earl Alexander of Tunis
William Kunstler: American attorney and civil rights activist (1919–1995)
A Russian lawyer-turned-politician who chaired the Duma's Family, Women and Children Affairs committee, she drew attention in 2012 for drafting controversial LGBT-related legislation — who is she?
Created in 1946 and headquartered in Paris, this government-owned utility operates 56 nuclear reactors across 18 sites and was the world's largest electricity producer in 2009 — which company?
Électricité de France: French multinational electric utility company.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was born first?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these came out first?
MUMPS (published 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Alessandro Volta is a physicist. Throughout his life, Volta enjoyed a certain amount of closeness with the emperor who conferred upon him numerous honours.
Which of these four is a chemist?
Samuel Conway is a chemist. Samuel Charles Conway (born June 4, 1965) is an American researcher in the pharmaceutical, biomedical and agrochemical fields of organic chemistry.
What is the atomic number of Lithium?
Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.
In what year was Blaise Pascal born?
Blaise Pascal (19 June 1623 – 19 August 1662) was a French mathematician, physicist, inventor, philosopher, and Catholic writer.
In what year was Friedrich Engels born?
Friedrich Engels: After Marx's death, Engels served as the editor of his works, completing the second and third volumes of Das Kapital.
In what year was Edward Teller born?
Edward Teller: Born in Austria-Hungary in 1908, Teller emigrated to the US in the 1930s, one of the many so-called "Martians", a group of Hungarian scientist émigrés.
In what year did J. Robert Oppenheimer die?
J. Robert Oppenheimer: In 1941, Oppenheimer was briefed about nuclear weapon design by Australian physicist Mark Oliphant.
In what year did Kitty Oppenheimer die?
Kitty Oppenheimer: Robert Oppenheimer, the director of the Manhattan Project's Los Alamos Laboratory during World War II.
In what year was Fructose discovered?
Fructose, or fruit sugar, is a common monosaccharide, i.e. a simple sugar.
In what year was Gallium discovered?
Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.
Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control
Lorazepam: Pfizer. Lorazepam, sold under the brand name Ativan among others, is a benzodiazepine medication.
Which country is AIDC F-CK-1 Ching-kuo from?
AIDC F-CK-1 Ching-kuo: Taiwan. The aircraft made its first flight in 1989.
Who is credited with discovering Plutonium?
Plutonium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
Who is credited with discovering Fermium?
Fermium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Fermium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fm and atomic number 100.
Who is credited with discovering Sodium?
Sodium: Humphry Davy. Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
Taken as a pill, cream, or injection, this antiviral medication is the go-to treatment for herpes simplex, chickenpox, and shingles — what is it?
Aciclovir is an antiviral medication. It is primarily used for the treatment of herpes simplex virus infections, chickenpox, and shingles.
This amphoteric compound forms a gelatinous precipitate in water and occurs naturally as the mineral gibbsite, one of bauxite's key components — what is it?
Aluminium hydroxide is a white chemical compound that is found as the mineral gibbsite (also known as hydrargillite) and its three much rarer polymorphs: bayerite, doyleite, and nordstrandite.
What term describes the discipline of measuring human body dimensions, applied everywhere from ergonomics and architecture to tracking historical living standards?
Anthropometry (from Ancient Greek (nthrpos) 'human' and (mtron) 'measure') refers to the measurement of the human individual.
This common vision condition occurs when the cornea or lens is slightly egg-shaped rather than spherical, causing blurred vision at any distance. What is it?
Astigmatism is a type of refractive error due to rotational asymmetry in the eye's refractive power.
Once chairman of the Nasdaq, this financier admitted to masterminding the largest-known Ponzi scheme in history, estimated at $65 billion — who was he?

Bernie Madoff (April 29, 1938 - April 14, 2021) was an American financier, con artist, and stock broker who was the admitted mastermind of the largest-known Ponzi scheme in history, worth an estimated $65 billion.
This branch of biology studies how plants have grown, reproduced, and evolved over the last 3.5 billion years of life on Earth — what field is it?
Botany is the branch of natural science and biology that studies the growth, reproduction and evolution of plants over the last 3.5 billion years of life on earth.
Its common name is a contraction of 'Mary's gold,' honoring the Virgin Mary, but this daisy-family genus's Latin name nods to the calendar instead — which flowering plant?
Calendula is a genus of about 15-20 species of annual and perennial herbaceous plants in the daisy family, Asteraceae that are often known as marigolds.
Their name is Greek for "head-feet," and fishers sometimes call them "inkfish" for their ink-squirting trick; squid, octopus and nautilus all belong. What's this molluscan class?
Cephalopod is any member of the molluscan class Cephalopoda (Greek plural, kephalpodes; "head-feet") such as a squid, octopus, cuttlefish, or nautilus.
This common name covers many species of bivalve mollusc that use a powerful foot to burrow into sand or mud, with two equal shells joined by adductor muscles — what creature is it?
Clam is a common name for several species of bivalve mollusc. In culinary usage, clams are commonly eaten marine bivalves, as in clam digging and the resulting soup, clam chowder.
A genus of over 260 fungi, most of them parasites that bore into insects and other arthropods, this 'club-headed' organism has 1,500 years of use in Chinese medicine — what is it?
Cordyceps is a genus of ascomycete fungi (sac fungi) that includes over 260 species worldwide, many of which are parasitic.
A staunch defender of Georg Cantor's set theory, this mathematician co-founded proof theory and became one of the most influential figures in his field — who is he?
David Hilbert (23 January 1862 - 14 February 1943) was a German mathematician and philosopher of mathematics and one of the most influential mathematicians of all time.
First proposed as a model organism in 1901, this tiny insect species has become biology's workhorse for genetics research, and it's the one buzzing around your rotting fruit bowl. Name the species?
Drosophila melanogaster is a species of fly (an insect of the order Diptera) in the family Drosophilidae.
Noted for producing one of the most variable litter sizes of any dog breed, this active gun dog comes in 'field' and 'house' varieties and gave rise to its American cousin breed — what is it?
English Cocker Spaniel is a breed of gun dog. It is noteworthy for producing one of the most varied numbers of pups in a litter among all dog breeds.
Colloquially called 'squirting,' this phenomenon involves fluid from the Skene's gland and is physiologically distinct from coital incontinence — what is it?
Female ejaculation is characterized as an expulsion of fluid from the Skene's gland at the lower end of the urethra during or before an orgasm.
Often bonded to glucose to form table sugar, this white, water-soluble simple sugar occurs naturally in honey, tree and vine fruits, and most root vegetables — name this sugar?
Fructose is a common monosaccharide, i.e.

Designed at a major tech company in 2007 by Robert Griesemer, Rob Pike, and Ken Thompson, this statically typed, compiled programming language borrows C-like syntax while adding garbage collection and built-in concurrency support — name the language?
Go (programming language) is a high-level, general-purpose programming language that is statically typed and compiled.
About the size of a closed fist and tucked between the lungs, this four-chambered muscular organ pumps blood throughout the body — name it?
Heart is a muscular organ found in humans and other animals.
Native to Japan, this deciduous shrub grows big flower heads that can turn pink or blue and is also known as the mophead or lacecap — which plant?
Hydrangea macrophylla is a species of flowering plant in the family Hydrangeaceae, native and endemic to Japan.
These creatures don't breathe through a nose or lungs — air enters through tiny paired openings along their sides, piped straight to the tissues. What hexapod group are they?
Insect (from Latin insectum) are hexapod invertebrates of the class Insecta.
Best known for his laws of planetary motion, this German astronomer has also been called the 'father of science fiction' for his novel Somnium. Who is he?
Johannes Kepler (27 December 1571 - 15 November 1630) was a German polymath who was an astronomer, mathematician, astrologer, natural philosopher and music theorist.
Which German engineer and economist founded the World Economic Forum in 1971 and chaired it until stepping down in 2025?
Klaus Schwab (born 30 March 1938) is a German mechanical engineer, economist, and founder of the World Economic Forum (WEF).
Named for the Latin word for weighing scales and lying between Virgo and Scorpius, this faint zodiac constellation has no first-magnitude stars — which one?
Libra (constellation) is a constellation of the zodiac and is located in the Southern celestial hemisphere.

While at IBM in the 1960s, this computer scientist invented a key technique behind the out-of-order execution most modern processors use — then was fired in 1968 for planning a gender transition, an act IBM apologized for in 2020. Who was this engineer?
Lynn Conway (January 2, 1938 - June 9, 2024) was an American computer scientist, electrical engineer, and transgender rights activist.

Awarded the 1918 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering energy quanta, this German theoretical physicist is considered the originator of quantum theory and one of the founders of modern physics — who is he?
Max Planck (23 April 1858 - 4 October 1947) was a German theoretical physicist.
This unit of time, normally equal to 60 seconds, can rarely stretch to 61 seconds under the UTC time standard because of a leap second — what is it?
Minute (symbol: min) is a unit of time defined as equal to 60 seconds.

This European twin-engine military helicopter was the first production helicopter ever built with entirely fly-by-wire flight controls, coming in both troop-transport and naval anti-submarine variants — what aircraft is it?
NHIndustries NH90 is a medium-sized European twin-engine multi-role military helicopter.
The smallest of its type, this Canadian gun dog has webbed feet and lures waterfowl to shore with playful antics before fetching them from the water — which breed is it?
Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever is a medium-sized gun dog bred primarily for hunting.

Created by Danish-Canadian programmer Rasmus Lerdorf in 1993 and released in 1995, this general-purpose scripting language was originally short for 'Personal Home Page' before becoming a recursive backronym — name the language?
PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
This inflammation of the lining of the abdominal cavity can be caused by a ruptured appendix, a perforated ulcer, or pancreatitis, and may lead to shock if untreated. What condition is it?
Peritonitis is inflammation of the localized or generalized peritoneum, the lining of the inner wall of the abdomen and covering of the abdominal organs.
Used in randomized clinical trials to gauge a treatment's true efficacy, this inert pill, injection, or sham surgery has no pharmaceutical effect of its own — what is it?
Placebo (pluh-) is a medicine or treatment intended to appear genuine to its recipient, but which has no pharmaceutical effect.

This mammal genus includes a familiar, masked, ring-tailed nocturnal visitor common across North America, plus two lesser-known tropical relatives; its closest kin are the ring-tailed cats and cacomistles. What animal is this?
Procyon (genus) is a genus of nocturnal mammals comprising three species commonly known as raccoons in the family Procyonidae.
A medium-sized tropical tree native to Southeast Asia, it's a close relative of the lychee and longan and shares its name with the edible fruit it bears — what is it?
Rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum) is a medium-sized tropical tree in the family Sapindaceae.
This woody perennial flowering plant, genus Rosa in the family Rosaceae, includes over 300 species and tens of thousands of cultivars, with sharp prickles on many stems — name the flower?
Rose is either a woody perennial flowering plant of the genus Rosa, in the family Rosaceae, or the flower it bears.
This synthetic element, atomic number 106, is so fleeting that only a few atoms exist at a time and decay within minutes — and it's named for an American nuclear chemist; what is it?
Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
Whether on land, in fresh water, or in the sea, this gastropod earns its name from a coiled shell roomy enough to fully retract into — what is it?
Snail is a shelled gastropod. The name is most often applied to land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod molluscs.

Starting with fever and flu-like symptoms before the skin blisters and peels into painful raw patches, this severe drug-triggered skin reaction sits on the same disease spectrum as toxic epidermal necrolysis, only less severe — which condition?
Stevens–Johnson syndrome (SJS) is a type of severe skin reaction.
Defined as applying conceptual knowledge to reach practical goals in a repeatable way, this field covers both tangible machines and intangible things like software — what is it?
Technology is the application of conceptual knowledge to achieve practical goals, especially in a reproducible way.
A nightshade-family relative of tobacco and the potato, this South American native arrived in Eurasia via the Columbian exchange and is botanically a berry eaten as a vegetable — what is it?
Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) is a plant whose fruit is an edible berry that is eaten as a vegetable.
This medical condition involves involuntary muscle spasms that interfere with vaginal intercourse or other penetration, often causing pain from the first attempt — what is it?
Vaginismus is a condition in which involuntary muscle spasm interferes with vaginal intercourse or other penetration of the vagina.
A physician and Royal Society charter member, he surveyed confiscated Irish land for Cromwell's soldiers but is best remembered for pioneering 'political arithmetic' in economics — who was he?
William Petty (26 May 1623 - 16 December 1687) was an English economist, physician, scientist and philosopher.
The first Muslim scientist to win a Nobel Prize, this Pakistani theoretical physicist shared the 1979 Physics prize for unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces — who was he?
First flown in October 1972, this was the world's first twin-engine wide-body airliner, born from a 1967 France-West Germany-UK collaboration that later lost its British partner — what is it?
Airbus A300: World's first twin-engine widebody jet airliner.
This three-star system includes Proxima, the closest star to the Sun, and shines as the third-brightest point in the night sky after Sirius and Canopus — which system?
Alpha Centauri: Star system in the Centaurus constellation.
Commonly called windflowers, which genus of the buttercup family is native to every continent except Australia, New Zealand, and Antarctica?
Anemone: Genus of flowering plants in the family Ranunculaceae.
Named for a mythological weaver transformed into a spider, which eight-legged class of arthropods includes scorpions, ticks, and mites?
Arachnid: Class of arthropods. The term is derived from the Greek word ἀράχνη (aráchnē, 'spider'), from the myth of the hubristic human weaver Arachne, who was turned into a spider.
This ocean giant, recorded at up to 680 kg, has vanished from the Black Sea but still roams the Mediterranean and both sides of another major ocean — which fish?
Atlantic bluefin tuna: Species of fish. The Atlantic bluefin tuna (Thunnus thynnus) is a species of tuna in the family Scombridae.

Developed in the 18th century by an English clergyman and, independently, by Pierre-Simon Laplace, this rule lets you flip a conditional probability — say, finding the odds a patient is sick given a positive test. What is it?
Bayes' theorem: Mathematical rule for inverting probabilities.
Prized for the rainbow, iridescent crust that forms when it oxidizes under heat, which brittle, silvery element is only 86 percent as dense as lead?
Bismuth: Chemical element with atomic number 83 (Bi)
Also nicknamed 'starflower,' this Mediterranean annual herb yields seed oil despite containing small amounts of toxic alkaloids — which plant?
Borage: Species of flowering plant in the family Boraginaceae.
One of the largest snake species on Earth, this Southeast Asian native became invasive in Florida after escaping the pet trade — which snake is this?
Burmese python: Species of large, nonvenomous snake.
Produced by chili peppers likely to deter hungry mammals, this hydrophobic compound is what gives them their burning, pungent kick — what is it?
Capsaicin: Pungent chemical compound in chili peppers. It is a potent irritant for mammals for which it produces a sensation of burning in any tissue with which it comes into contact.

This biological process splits a parent into two daughters, either producing genetically identical copies via mitosis or reducing chromosome number by half via meiosis to form gametes. What process is it?
Cell division: Biological process. Cell division usually occurs as part of a larger cell cycle in which the cell grows and replicates its chromosome(s) before dividing.
Known for a bitter metallic aftertaste that gets worse if you rinse with water, this antiseptic is used before surgery and to prevent dental plaque — what is it?
Chlorhexidine: Disinfectant and antiseptic. Chlorhexidine is a disinfectant and antiseptic which is used for skin disinfection before surgery and to disinfect surgical instruments.

First discovered as an atypical antipsychotic, this medication is reserved for schizophrenia patients who haven't responded to two other drugs, and is also used for psychosis linked to Parkinson's disease — what is it?
Clozapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Clozapine, sold under the brand name Clozaril among others, is a psychiatric medication and was the first atypical antipsychotic to be discovered.
These wind-pollinated, cone-bearing evergreens dominated Earth's landscapes throughout the Mesozoic before flowering plants took over — what group of plants is this?
Conifer: Group of seed plants. As of 2025, 94 conifer species are listed as endangered and 30 as critically endangered.
Their Latin name means 'those with shells,' and this mostly aquatic group includes crabs, lobsters, krill, barnacles, and mantis shrimp — what are they?
Named for a 19th-century British mathematician, this pair of logic rules shows how 'and' and 'or' swap places under negation — what are they called?
De Morgan's laws: Pair of logical equivalences.

Sudden lower-abdominal pain, sometimes a 'smoldering' slow burn over days — and the trouble is little abnormal pouches inflaming in the wall of your large intestine. What gastrointestinal disease is this?
Diverticulitis: Digestive disease of the large intestine. People may experience a single attack, repeated attacks, or ongoing "smoldering" diverticulitis.
Also known as dropsy, this medical condition involves fluid buildup in body tissue, often causing swelling in the legs or arms — what is it?
Edema: Accumulation of excess fluid in tissue.
This outermost skin layer ranges from about 31 micrometers thick on delicate areas to nearly 600 micrometers on the sole of the foot — what is it?
Epidermis: Outermost of the three layers that make up the skin.

One of the few birds known to pass the mirror test, this highly intelligent corvid found across the northern reaches of Eurasia has a nidopallium proportionally as large as a chimpanzee's brain — which bird is it?
Eurasian magpie: Species of bird. The Eurasian magpie or common magpie (Pica pica) is a resident breeding bird throughout the northern part of the Eurasian continent.

Named for the physicist who reportedly asked 'but where is everybody?' at Los Alamos in 1950, this puzzle questions why we've found no evidence of alien civilizations despite the odds favoring them — what's it called?
Fermi paradox: Discrepancy of the lack of evidence for alien life despite its apparent likelihood.
Called the "father of modern parasitology," this Italian physician-poet famously dismantled spontaneous generation by showing that maggots hatch from fly eggs — who was he?
Francesco Redi: Italian naturalist and poet. Francesco Redi (18 February 1626 – 1 March 1697) was an Italian physician, naturalist, biologist, and poet.
Once Mexico's top law-enforcement official as secretary of public security, this man was convicted in a Brooklyn courtroom in 2023 for taking millions in bribes from the Sinaloa Cartel — who is he?
Genaro García Luna: Mexican politician and convicted felon (born 1968)
Caused by iodine deficiency in over 90% of cases worldwide, this neck swelling results from an enlarged thyroid gland — what's the condition called?
Goitre: Neck swelling due to enlarged thyroid gland. A goitre (British English, spelled goiter in American English) is a swelling in the neck resulting from an enlarged thyroid gland.

Named from Greek words meaning 'naked seed,' this group of woody plants — including conifers, cycads, and ginkgos — lacks the protective covering that encloses a flowering plant's seeds. What is it called?
Gymnosperm: Clade of non-flowering, naked-seeded vascular plants.
This Dutch-born entrepreneur produced Japan's first major turn-based role-playing game and later secured the console distribution rights to a Russian puzzle game called Tetris — who is he?
Henk Rogers: Dutch-born American computer programmer (born 1953)
Despite the name, this 'living fossil' is no crustacean at all — it's a chelicerate, kin to spiders and scorpions, and its three-part body ends in a spiky tail called a telson. What creature is it?
Horseshoe crab: Family of basal chelicerates.
This mammal order today includes only small African and Middle Eastern hyraxes, but once boasted a species weighing up to 600 kilograms called Titanohyrax — which order?
Hyracoidea: Order of mammals. It includes the living hyraxes, placed within the family Procaviidae, and several extinct taxa.
She and her husband won the 1935 Nobel in Chemistry for discovering induced radioactivity — making her half of the only mother-daughter pair to both win Nobel Prizes. Who is this scientist?
Irène Joliot-Curie: French chemist and physicist (1897–1956)

This temporary condition throws your internal body clock out of sync with local time after rapid travel across multiple time zones — and most people find it harder to shake off flying east than west — what is it?

Jet lag: Condition due to travel across time zones. The phase shift when travelling from east to west is referred to as phase-delay of the circadian cycle, whereas going west to east is phase-advance of the cycle.

Known to NATO by the reporting name Hokum A and nicknamed 'Black Shark' for its distinctive coaxial rotors, this Russian single-seat attack helicopter has a rare rescue ejection system — which aircraft?
Kamov Ka-50: Attack helicopter. It was designed in the 1980s and adopted for service in the Russian army in 1995.
With a toothed, funnel-like sucking mouth, this jawless fish's name may derive from Latin for 'stone licker,' and it's genetically closer to hagfish than to any jawed vertebrate — what is it?
Lamprey: Class of jawless fish. Lampreys (sometimes inaccurately called lamprey eels) are a group of jawless fish composing the order Petromyzontiformes, sole order in the class Petromyzontida.
This genus of bulb-grown flowering plants, prized for their large blooms, is highly toxic to cats — even though many unrelated plants borrow its common name — which genus?
Lilium: Genus of plants. Lilium ( LIL-ee-əm) is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants growing from bulbs, all with large and often prominent flowers.
Originating in 1993 and written in ANSI C, this lightweight scripting language was designed to be embedded inside other applications — which language?
Lua: Lightweight programming language. Lua is a lightweight, high-level, multi-paradigm programming language designed mainly for embedded use in applications.
Sharing joints only with the temporal bones, this is the skull's lone movable bone, hosting the lower teeth and shrinking in size since humans began farming around 10,000 BCE — what is it called?
Mandible: Lower jaw bone. The mandible hosts the lower teeth (their depth delineated by the alveolar process).
Its name means 'big tooth,' and this extinct giant mackerel shark — once mistaken for a great white relative — is known only from fragmentary remains. What is it?
Megalodon: Extinct giant shark species. Megalodon probably had a major impact on the structure of marine communities.

This medical condition, usually diagnosed shortly after birth, is defined as a length at least 2.5 standard deviations below the average and affects about 1.5 in 10,000 male newborns in North America. What is this condition?
First prepared in 1908 by biochemist Kikunae Ikeda as he tried to bottle the savory taste of kombu seaweed, this flavor enhancer is the original source of umami in cooking — what is it?
Monosodium glutamate: Flavor enhancer (621 or E621)
Made by giving a paper loop a half-twist before joining the ends, this non-orientable surface first appeared in Roman mosaics — what is it called?
Möbius strip: Non-orientable surface with one edge.
This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats acute pain and osteoarthritis by blocking prostaglandins, though it carries a notable risk of liver problems — what is it?
Nimesulide: Anti-inflammatory drug. Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with pain medication and fever reducing properties.
This British engineer rewrote Maxwell's equations into the form we use today and devised the telegrapher's equations — who was he?
Oliver Heaviside: British mathematician and electrical engineer (1850–1925)

Though isolated observations date back to the 6th century BC, this science's modern foundation is credited to Georges Cuvier's 1796 work demonstrating that species could go extinct — what field is this?
Paleontology: Study of past life through fossils.
Derived from Greek words meaning 'healer of children,' this branch of medicine covers care from infancy through adolescence — what is it?
Pediatrics: Branch of medicine caring for children. Within the Commonwealth, pediatrics covers patients until the age of 18, except in India where the pediatric age is 12.

Nicknamed 'banana spiders' and 'armed spiders' for their aggressive posture, this genus found mainly in northern South America is better known by a name describing its roaming habits — what genus is this?
Its name comes from the Greek for 'making,' and it leans on devices like assonance, alliteration, and metre to evoke meanings beyond the literal — what literary art is this?

Detected by receptors in your muscles, tendons, and joints, this sense tells your brain where your body is in space, working alongside vision and balance to keep you upright and coordinated — what's it called?
Proprioception: Sense of self-movement, force, and body position.
Found in notable amounts in capers, red onions, and kale, this bitter-tasting plant flavonol is a popular ingredient in dietary supplements — what compound?
Quercetin: Chemical compound. It is found in many fruits, vegetables, leaves, seeds, and grains; capers, red onions, and kale are common foods containing appreciable amounts of it.

Found in fish, dairy, and meat, this fat-soluble vitamin A derivative is prescribed for xerophthalmia and used topically in anti-wrinkle skincare — but too much during pregnancy can harm the fetus. What is it?
Once used by German butchers to herd cattle and pull meat carts to market, this mastiff-type breed now works as a search-and-rescue and police dog — which breed?
Rottweiler: Large German dog breed. The Rottweiler (UK also, German: [ˈʁɔtvaɪ̯lɐ]) is a breed of domestic mastiff type dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large.

Discovered in 1879 via spectral analysis of Scandinavian minerals, this silvery-white rare-earth element with atomic number 21 wasn't isolated in metallic form until 1937, and today it's prized for strengthening aluminum alloys — which element?
Scandium: Chemical element with atomic number 21 (Sc)
This body of religious law, drawn from the Qur'an and hadith, refers to immutable divine law — distinct from fiqh, its human interpretation by scholars. What is it?
Sharia: Islamic law. Approaches to Sharia in the 21st century vary widely, and the role and mutability of Sharia in a changing world has become an increasingly debated topic in Islam.

Historically mined in vast deposits and nicknamed 'Chile saltpeter,' this white, water-soluble alkali metal compound is used in fertilizers, fireworks, meat preservation, and solid rocket fuel. What is it?
Sodium nitrate: Chemical compound. The mineral form is also known as nitratine, nitratite or soda niter.
